he who is named Mahāsamudra and Mahāparvata as well.
The seed-syllable *hūṃ* is proclaimed as "mahāściśceti," and *hrīṃ* is celebrated as the power (*śakti*).
One should perform the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of Lajjā using [the syllables] conjoined with the six long vowels.

Then, with a perfectly steady mind, the practitioner of mantra should meditate upon the deities of the mantra as being adorned with various jewels and considered to be dripping with water from the trees.
One should meditate upon the mountain as being filled with beasts such as tigers and endowed with sacred measures (mānas),
abounding in seeds such as the fish and the tortoise, and adorned with the nine jewels.
He should contemplate the ocean with its dense masses and surging waves,
and the wondrous triple world completely overwhelmed by garlands of flames.
For the pacification of enemies, one should meditate upon the great fire as being yellow in color,
arising from the first letter of the vowels (A), soiled, and obstructing the earth and sky.
One should contemplate the Fire of Digestion (Pacana) as the life-force of the universe, existing in the form of vital breath (prāṇa),
which is crowded with villages and filled with rivers, mountains, trees, and other such things.
The earth, which is the support of the world, should be meditated upon as being within the *pṛthvīṃha* [syllable] by one who possesses the wisdom of the *antima* [final letter];
it is endowed with the sun and other planets, the lunar mansions, and the wheel of time (*kālacakra*).
One should meditate on the stainless sky, which provides a refuge for all living beings;
having thus meditated upon the six deities, one should [recite] sixteen thousand times.
One should recite the mantra ten times the number of oblations and perform the fire sacrifice (*homa*) with six substances:
rice grains, husked rice, clarified butter, mustard seeds, hibiscus flowers, and sesame seeds.

Having offered these according to their respective portions, one should worship on the previously mentioned seat with the limbs and so forth, and with Vajra and the others; thus the mantra becomes perfected.
Warding off the assault of enemies, one should worship the mantra there according to the rule:
[visualizing] the letter 'A' in the form of a mountain, rushing toward the enemy.
One should contemplate in the eastern direction the extremely fierce letter *ka*, facing upward,
which represents hunger and a great wave that has inundated the entire surface of the earth.
One should contemplate the formidable one in the form of the ocean in the western direction;
the fourth and fifth primordial atoms have the forms of the earth and the element of space, respectively.
When one subdues the host of enemies and the ocean of bondage for oneself, then, O enemy, that pair of syllables [the name] becomes the path of the breath of misfortune.
One should meditate on the mantra without its base (nirādhāna), causing the enemy to be overwhelmed;
[one should visualize] the three syllables beginning with Māyā (Hrīṃ) at the enemy's eyes, ears, and mouth.
The best of practitioners should meditate on each [weapon] individually as it obstructs;
the weapon, agitated by the armor-mantra, [should be visualized] from the base-region of the enemy.
Having kindled the fire and anointed that body, he should meditate upon the mantra;
thus he should meditate on the letters and recite the mantra consisting of a thousand syllables.
One who performs this rite through the mastery of breath-control (prāṇāyāma) and other means certainly meditates upon the enemy within a distance of three maṇḍalas.
Thus, one who performs such action through breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), recitation (*japa*), and so forth,
having thoroughly purified his own self, should meditate upon Hari for the sake of his own protection and other purposes.
In the water, in the fire, in the heart, in the sun, on the sacrificial ground,
and in images— in these six places, the proper worship of Hari is said to be appropriate.
For Hari is indeed within the mantra of water; therefore, Hari is always in the waters. Viṣṇu, as Hari, resides in the heart of yogis through the presence of the fire-ritual.
For the wise, Hari is in the sun; for those of purified soul, he is on the sacrificial ground;
for those of limited intellect, he is in the image—thus are the sixfold forms remembered.
I shall describe the characteristics of those [lines] which are natural and artificial, immovable and movable, and devoid of life and endowed with life.
The naturally formed *sālagrāma* is of two kinds and is purifying;
in its absence, the discus from Dvārakā is likewise purifying.
The artificial [images] are said to be of ten kinds; among them, each preceding type is superior to the one following it.
The first types may be fashioned from jewels, gold, or even silver.
Born of copper, born of bell-metal, born of crystal, born of red and cool [substances],
born of wood, born of clay, and likewise of variegated form— in this sequence.
The Kṣatriya forms are indeed immovable, just as Haridvāra is like Gayā;
those images fashioned by the deities are both movable and immovable.
Jagannātha, Ekadeśa, Pāṇḍuraṅga, and others are likewise praised;
living beings are considered Brāhmaṇas, cows, and lifeless objects are known as Pippalas (the sacred fig tree).
First, one should perform the mantra-nyāsa upon one's own body and the deities;
then, with the limbs consecrated by the Gāyatrī and the Oṃkāra, one should worship the imperishable Viṣṇu.
O Goddess, when worship is performed at Kāśī, it bestows all accomplishments;
however, the merit on the summit of the Vindhya mountain is twice as great as that.
Whatever fruit is obtained at Gaṅgā, Gayā, Kurukṣetra, Prabhāsa, Bhāskara, as well as in the Naimiṣa forest and other such places on the Vindhya mountain;
Twice that merit is obtained in the presence of Puruṣottama;
four times that merit is obtained in the waters of the Karatoyā river.
Twice that merit is obtained by bathing in the Lohitya river;
a hundred times that merit is obtained at Kāmākhyā in the Yonimaṇḍala.
Twice that merit is obtained on the head of Nīlakaṇṭha;
ten million times that merit is obtained in Nepāla, in the Guhyamaṇḍala.
By the offering of even a single flower, one obtains fruit equal to Mount Sumeru;
by the offering of a single drop of water, one obtains the fruit of the seven oceans.
In the sacred seat of Guhyeśvarī, there is nothing within the circle of the universe;
the three mudrās for the fire-oblation are said to be Mṛgī, Haṃsī, and Śūkarī.
The *śūkarī* (pig) mudrā is the contraction [of the fingers]; the *mṛgī* (deer) mudrā is the little finger;
and the *haṃsī* (swan) mudrā is the index finger extended—thus the three mudrās are proclaimed.
O Supreme Goddess, [this applies] in rites for pacification and nourishment, as well as for killing and expulsion, and likewise for causing enmity, immobilization, and subjugation.
In rites of pacification (śāntika), she should be known as a doe; in rites of enrichment (pauṣṭika), as a goose;
in rites of malevolent magic (abhicāra), she should be a sow; and in rites such as inciting hatred and expulsion, she is likewise.
The gods do not accept an oblation that is devoid of mudrās. That dull-witted person who, out of delusion, desires to offer an oblation lacking the mudrās [is mistaken].

For subjugation (vaśya) and pacification (śānti), a golden vessel or an earthen vessel is used; for immobilization (staṃbhana), that same [earthen] one; for causing enmity (vidveṣa), a vessel made of khadira wood; and for eradication (uccāṭa), a vessel measured in iron.
For killing, there should be a hen’s egg; these are the vessels for the propitiatory rite.
Bhairava said:
O Mother Goddess, Mahāmāyā, who brings about bondage and liberation! Now I desire to hear the most excellent lineage of gurus.
The Goddess said:
The lineage of gurus is indeed manifold due to the weight of the extensive mantras;
how could time itself be beginningless? How then can I describe that to you?
If the family group does not know [this], they will become lost from the path;
for one who is lost from the path, the knowledge of mantras does not come within the range of such results.
If there is no succession of gurus and disciples,
then the yantras, tantras, and vidyās will undoubtedly be ineffective.
Even one who has twenty, nineteen, seventeen, or three [generations],
yet does not know the lineages of the gurus, is called a "disciple" whose lineage is lost.
The lineage of the Guru should be known as most wonderful and superior to one's own lineage;
O Maheśvara, the giver of mantra should be known as even more superior than one's father.
Therefore, O Lord of Gods, listen briefly to these teachers in every case:
first, O Lord of Gods, everywhere the giver of the mantra is the primary teacher.
You are indeed the supreme and subordinate guru, while I am the Parameṣṭhin;
in all the Tantras and Vidyās, you yourself are the one who manifests as Prakṛti.
Then [he sees] the form of the Supreme Person (Puruṣa), then his own guru and the lineage [of gurus];
likewise, those who bite with frost (Himadaṃśa) and especially those devoted to me.
O God, these hosts of divine gurus and likewise the hosts of perfected gurus bestow success everywhere at the forefront of all mantras.
I shall briefly describe the lineages of men before you;
therein lies the goddess Kālikā—listen now to her lineage of gurus.
Mahādevī, Mahādeva, Tripurā, and Bhairava are declared to be the gurus of the Divine Current (divyaugha); now I shall describe the gurus of the Siddha Current (siddhaugha).
Brahmānanda, Pūrṇa, Carata, Sulocana, Kumāra, Krodhana, Varada, and Smaradīpana.
Listen, O beloved, to the multitudes of men: Māyā and Māyāvatī, as well as Vimala, Kuśala, Bhīmasena, and Sudhākara.
Mīna, Gorakṣaka, Bhojadeva, Prajāpati, Mūladeva, Avantideva, Vighneśa, and Hutāśana.
Samaya, Ānanda, and Saṃtoṣā are remembered as the Gurus;
she who possesses the digit (kalā) in the form of sound [arises] from the state of emptiness through the nature of emptiness.
Established therein, that stage of Dharma is known by the wise as supremely fierce;
it is always characterized by the states of wrath, command, passion, delusion, and the roar of destruction.
This entire world is known as the ground of the Rava-teya mantra;
it is free from accumulation, lack of taste, improper conduct, and verbal expression.
The wise know that for all those who practice, this is their ground;
in the staff there are four staves, and from the staff they proceed to two staves.
That which is distinguished by the equality of phonemes is known as the ground of mantra;
it is free from the grasping of "kahīnā" and so forth, and is unagitated by the destruction of time and non-time.

All mantras are contained within the *kalā*; that is known as the ground of mantra (*mantrabhūmi*). It is all-pervasive in form yet abides in formlessness; it transcends form and is beyond the senses.
That stage of mantra is known by the wise as being divided into hundreds of forms;
first, through the radiance of intuitive insight (*pratibhā*), it becomes ever-shifting and unsteady.
The wise know that state of the word "niḥsvabhāva" (absence of intrinsic nature) to be the stage of mantra;
it vibrates without directions, situated between the imperishable and the perishable.
The wise know that the ground of mantra is cultivated through the state of Great Abiding;
it is always free from mental states such as pride and is devoid of both arrogance and dejection.
Because it possesses the nature of the eye of Mananetra, the wise know that to be the ground of mantra;
it is mounted upon the syllable *ka* and the goddess Kamalā, and rests within the hollow of the parrot’s beak.
That which is the digit (kalā) that gives birth to time is known as the ground of mantra;
it has instantly entered within, and here it consists of eight parts abiding in the void.
The individual soul (vyaṣṭi) is the limit of its own essential nature; the wise know that to be the plane of mantra.
It always devours all the fires of anger with constant longing.
O wise one, that stage of mantra is merged within all existents;
it is the pervasive state of all things, and it is intent upon forcibly seizing the power of Hara.
The wise know that state to be the ground of mantra, characterized by the supreme bliss of the swift-moving [āśava],
which is free from the extremes of the seen and the unseen.
O wise one, that ground of mantra vibrates in the supreme ether;
it consists of the knowledge of the inner self, is tranquil by nature, supreme, and imperishable.
It is known as the stage of mantra, which is free from coarseness, unshakable, and peaceful;
it is liberated from both sides, being neither middle nor non-middle.
Established there, she plays; that is known as the ground of mantra.
She is downward-facing, desireless, and the devourer of both time and non-time.
Beyond mantras and ignorant of mantras, the wise know that to be the stage of mantra;
it is always sixteen-fold, beginning with the two and ending with ten.
They know that which lacks measure to be the ground of the secret mantra;
it is the depth of reality, yet devoid of both reality and unreality.
The wise know that stage of mantra, however, to be characterized by the three principles (tritatva),
wherein there is no higher knowledge, and wherein knowledge is both supreme and non-supreme.
Where the three wombs are cast out, that is known by the wise as the ground of mantra;
she who has the form of Rākā and the nature of Kuhū, and who devours the space of Kuhū and Rākā.
Delighting in the nature of others, that wise one is indeed on the stage of mantra;
subtle within and subtle without, she moves through all that is mobile and immobile.
O Khareśvarī, that which is formless is always form; that is the ground of mantra for the wise, which has gradually transcended into the supreme form.
That ground of mantra is indeed known by the wise as the source of all mantras;
it is the syllable-less source of mantra, the great mantra of the three families.
The progenitor of the meaning of all mantras is the great *bindu*, which is beyond syllables;
it is the five-syllabled great void, the *bindu*-void, and the hundred-syllabled.
He is the creator of all, yet formless; he holds the sixteen and the half-moon bindu;
he is stainless, beyond all parts (kalās), and sustains the pinnacle of the fourth dhyāna.
Possessing the mastery of all meditative concentrations and supernormal knowledges, and knowing the family and lineage of samādhis,
one should grasp the samādhi when it serves as the cause for all enjoyments.
I bow down to Karavīrā, who dwells in the cremation ground; to the supreme Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī; to Caṇḍā, Pratyaṅgirā, and Kālī; and to Siddhilakṣmī.
One should prepare eight hundred and one [offerings] consisting of bliss in successive order,
as well as the sacrificial porridge (caru) and the great lamp, which have been handed down through the lineage of tradition.
Without the three [vessels], there is no accomplishment even in hundreds of millions of eons—
whether it be a heap of grain in a great vessel, or a jar filled with wine.
And for one who is constantly devoted to worship, that [merit] shall become inexhaustible,
O beloved, whether by means of a lamp kindled with great oil or with fish oil.
There, having worshipped the Goddess according to the prescribed rite one hundred and eight times,
[one should employ] a wick for the sake of pacification, nourishment, and the destruction of diseases and the like.
For the rite of eradication (*uccāṭana*), she is smoke-colored; for subjugation (*vaśya*), she is black and red;
for killing (*māraṇa*), she is black-colored; and for the purpose of causing disease, she is black-colored.
In inciting enmity, she is five-colored; in paralyzing, yellow;
for the sake of victory, reddish-white; and in union, like a ray of light.
The practitioner endowed with devotion attains all desires;
O Maheśvarī, O Devikā, O Kāmakalā, O Kālī, grant your permission!
O beloved, I shall strive for the sake of achieving security and prosperity at the edge of this region; furthermore, for those capable Śaivas, there shall be two sectarian marks (tilakas).
At first, there should be the triple mark (tripuṇḍra) with ashes, and not another with sandalwood paste.
[He is] the glory of all faces, the neck, and the one dwelling in the cave of the heart of all beings.
The Blessed One is all-pervading; therefore, Śiva is omnipresent.
O Goddess, the mind became always overcome by sin and was non-natural.
"O you whose essence is the extraction of that [impurity], remove the evil, phaṭ! Homage!
Purification is considered to be of two kinds: the general and the specific."
The general [purification] has been briefly described; the specific [purification] is very extensive.
One should purify the six cakras beginning with Kuṇḍalinī and ending with Ājñā.
By purifying that [body], the entire physical frame attains purity;
when that is purified, rituals such as ritual placement (nyāsa), worship (pūjā), and recitation (japa) become truly pure.
With a great amount of phalgu powder and a great amount of red pigment,
one should illuminate the bowl, the islands, and so forth with a great quantity of oil at night in every way.
The Vidyā of seventeen syllables is the sovereign of the lords of Vidyā and Avidyā;
she is renowned as Siddhikālī, the supreme lordess who is the fortune of accomplishment (Siddhilakṣmī).
One should diligently perform the external worship with the *caru* (sacrificial rice) for the supreme and the middling deities;
however, within the house, one should always perform the *caru* worship for the supreme deity residing in the center of the external [mandala].
In this tantra, Siddhilakṣmī, Jayadratha, Guhyakālī, Rājalakṣmī, and Śivāpraty-aṅgirā have been fully described.
There is no auspicious knowledge equal to this, which accomplishes all rites;
this knowledge is the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā), remembered as the collection of garland-mantras.
And this [teaching] is not given to them as something acquired through effort, but rather it is illuminated by its own nature;
O Goddess, just as it is in you, so shall it become equal within my body.
One should hold the body, head, and neck straight and motionless;
looking at the tip of the nose, one should not look toward the directions.
Marrow, fat, grease, testicles, flesh, and blood—one should offer these;
it destroys another Yoginī along with all her attendants.

"To those who are devoted to the Guru, the Devas, and the Fire, and who are intent upon mantra and meditation—there, in their midst, [the offering] should be given; such is the command of the Supreme Lord."
The goddess Tripurā resides in Ājñā; Kubjikā in Mūlādhāra; Caṇḍeśvarī in Svādhiṣṭhāna; and Guhyakālikā in Anāhata.
In the Maṇipūraka cakra, Chinnamastā is proclaimed;
in the Viśuddha, Rājamātaṅgī—these are the presiding deities of the cakras.
The [six directions] known as upward, west, east, north, downward, and south are as follows:
just as Tāleśvarī is Pūrṇā, so Nisā is Pūrṇeśvarī.
Just as Niseśvarī is Kubjā, so too are the Guhyakas Kubjas;
she is the illustrious Mahātparā, the Great Vidyā, Mahātripurasundarī.
The great mantra *Praprasāda* is both with parts (*sakala*) and without parts (*niṣkala*). One's own body is said to be with parts, while the supreme primordial principles are without parts.
Having understood [the deity] as both with parts (sakala) and without parts (niṣkala), one should worship with the disposition of liberation.
These six traditions (ṣaḍāmnāya) have been proclaimed; in that [system], the presiding goddesses (mānāyikāḥ) follow in sequence.
Each mantra is one, each placement (nyāsa) is one, and likewise meditation is one;
the recitation (japa) should be one hundred and eight, or half of that, or even a quarter.
Within the Western Tradition (Paścimāmnāya), Kubjikā is indeed considered the principal deity;
the Mūlādhāra cakra is her abode for the purpose of her dwelling.
One should meditate upon Kubjikā in the great wheel at the root-support (mūlādhāra).
Kuṇḍalinī, the power of Brahman, resides in the lotus of the foundation.
This [nāḍī], which bestows immortality, leads [the breath] invariably up to the aperture of Brahmā;
from Kuṇḍalinī, this entire world of moving and non-moving beings has arisen.
The second [system] describes the world-form and the material body as well as primordial nature (prakṛti) and the spirit (puruṣa); this is Sāṃkhya-Yoga.

Just as [the Lord] is the cause of the world, so too is He the cause of both bondage and liberation. In that regard, *prakṛti* (primordial nature) comes first, and the *puruṣa* (spirit) follows immediately after it.
For Prakṛti is indeed of the nature of Śakti, while Puruṣa is called Śiva;
the primordial Śakti is Kuṇḍalinī, who is Prakṛti consisting of consciousness and the creative power (kalā).
These and many other expressive words found within the scope of the scriptures [denote the Supreme]:
Paramātman, Īśvara, Sākṣin, Māyeśa, Puruṣa, and Śiva.
These are also numerous synonymous terms for the Supreme Lord.
Her abode is called the "bulb" (kanda) because it is the foundational support for her root.
It is known as the Mūlādhāra, likewise bound by the knot of Brahmā;
there, it has the form of a sleeping serpent, encircled by eight coils.
Causing the entire body to move, she remains there in the form of nectar;
the abode of Sadāśiva is known as the Brahma-randhra.
Upon that is a thousand-petaled lotus, facing downward;
there, within the aperture of the *brahmarandhra*, resides Kuṇḍalinī in her embodied form.
Having entered, it remains at the *brahmarandhra*; from there, it proceeds to the mouth. The *brahmarandhra* is located in the head, and the *brahmagranthi* is above the anus.
Because it is the knot that brings about liberation, it is known as the Brahma-knot;
the eternal Brahma-knot is located at the root-support (mūlādhāra) and the bulb (kanda).
The words "the cosmic egg" (brahmāṇḍa), "the bed of Brahmā" (brahmaśayyā), and "the enclosure" (parya) are synonyms;
for it is indeed within Kuṇḍalinī that [the breath] always ascends toward the presence of Śiva.
Śiva never indeed comes near her;
wherever she goes after resting along the path of the immortal Liṅga.
Because it moves upward and is situated above all, it is called the *cakra*;
O Goddess Kālikā, you are the digit of desire (*kāmakalā*) who brings about creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
p.
87a) Here, indeed, is the consecration performed together with the retinue,
for your sake, prepared according to one's ability and according to what has been obtained.
O Goddess, fix your gaze upon all these articles of worship:
the water, the unguent, the flower, the incense, the lamp, and likewise the food offering.
Furthermore, regarding the food offering, the betel-roll, and likewise the royal regalia—
even when these are presided over by you alone, they protect [the ritual] from obstacles in every way.
All beings shall flee from me, I shall have protection,
and all my desires shall be fulfilled through your grace.
O Goddess, by the power of your compassion, this worship shall become fruitful;
having made a seat of human skin, one should perform the worship using a human skull as the vessel.
Just as one should purify [the vessel] with non-conceptual awareness as instructed by the mouth of the Guru,
it is filled with that which resembles the juice of lac, for no other reason.
Having offered worthless things there into a vessel filled with the causal substance,
specifically on the eighth, the fourteenth, or the ninth lunar day;
Likewise, on Śivarātri, one should perform worship during the night;
indeed, one should carry out everything exactly as in the worship of the Śrīcakra.
One should place the great vessel within the triangle of the bindu-cakra;
and in the five-spoked [cakra] of Pañcakālī, one should place the caru offering five times in succession.
O blessed lady, there is nothing higher than this in the worship of the Kālikākrama;
heaven, enjoyment, happiness, liberation, the command, and accomplishment will certainly be attained.
Truth, truth, O Great Goddess, I speak this as the truth:
he who acts otherwise, through the fallacious reasoning of causal arguments and sophistry, [is a fool].
He would obtain only exhaustion and not attain success;
[the goddesses] Maṅgalā, Mahāmāyā, Caṇḍakāpālinī, and Śivā.
Cāmuṇḍā, Carcikā, Caṇḍā, she who effects creation, maintenance, and end;
the Ineffable, the Fortunate One, the Secret Kālī, Jayā, and the Supreme.
She is known as Siddhilakṣmī, Viśvalakṣmī, and Mahāpratyamgirā;
she is Sundarī, Tripurā, Cāru, Ugrā, Caṇḍā, and Prakāśinī.
She has become divided in many ways and rests upon various distinctions;
she is one yet possesses many forms—one should know her through the divine eye.
He alone is the best of practitioners, a vessel for the knowledge of accomplishment;
[he masters] space, wind, fire, water, and likewise earth.
O beloved, that science named Rāvaṇī bestows both liberation and worldly enjoyment;
it is remembered as the supreme single-syllabled science (ekākṣarī) that grants both enjoyment and liberation.
Śikhī (Ś), Madhuhā (Kha), Yuktā (Phreṃ), and Kālī (M) are declared to be Prāṇa;
having written Mātmaka (Khphreṃ), one should write Mahācaṇḍa (Matā).
Having bestowed the station of Yogeśvarī, this nine-syllabled Vidyā is renowned as the Mother of Mantras, the bestower of sovereignty over the three worlds.
She is the mother of all mantras, the channel through which all mantras flow;
she is the mantra-mother who flows forth in manifold ways.
Pratyaṅgirā Mahākālī is the bestower of the bliss of liberation;
listen now to those sixteen-syllable vidyās which are the very life-force.
By the mere instruction of which one becomes fit for the status of Brahmā;
having extracted the three syllables, one should then write the "Great Roar" (mahārāva).
O Goddess worshipped by the thirty [gods], the night joined with Mādhava should be known as such;
when Satya has ascended, it is swallowed by the eternal one through his fourfold nature.
Having ascended through the true and the true, one becomes a Kevalin, a master of the Śikṣma;
thereafter, one is endowed with the Cakrin, the Jaṭhara, and Nārāyaṇa.
Joined with Mādhava, O younger brother of Vala, one should write again;
then one should write Māyā, Caṇḍī, Kūrca, Rakṣā, and Mahārāva once more.
The Goddess should employ Rati and recite the Head-mantra;
this is declared to be the sixteenth syllable, proclaimed as the King of Mantras.
O Goddess of gods, a single recitation [of this] is equal to ten million Vājapeya sacrifices,
thousands of Aśvamedha sacrifices, and likewise the circumambulation of the entire earth.
The merit arising from bathing at Prayāga when the sun is situated in Makara is said to be increased a hundredfold by the worship of Kālikā according to the prescribed rite.
The merit that is obtained by sequentially visiting the holy hermitages is equal to the merit of the dharma of the four castes through the worship of Kālikā.

O Goddess of Devas, performing a pilgrimage to Kāśī and other holy sites, accompanied by three and a half crores [of attendants], is equal to the tulā-dāna; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
O Goddess of gods, by reciting [her mantra] one hundred thousand times, what more need be said regarding one who shall become a possessor of siddhi—
by whose power the fourteen worlds [are sustained] by the Goddess?
The goddess known as Pratyaṅgirā was created by Kṛtānta for the sake of gentle accomplishment;
indeed, with the consent of Nārada, the name of the goddess was made twofold.
O Goddess, in the city called Śoṇita, within the form of Hari and Śaṅkara,
he bestowed it upon Kṛṣṇa by means of Nārada, the lord of sages.

In ancient times, Hari, having been entreated by Hara, offered [the mantra] for the sake of Vāsudeva’s beloved and for his protection, after performing sacrifices in the regions of Hariṇāṭṭa and Ambhaṣṭra.
Just as a flower enjoyed by a bee becomes fit for Śiva,
so too is the ineffable reality (nirakṣara-vastu) conjoined with syllables (akṣara).
O Goddess, one should not cause the extraction [of the mantra] to be written down, for she is the supreme Mistress of Phonemes (Varṇeśvarī) in person;
indeed, a curse will surely follow, and the destruction of the mantra will arise.
Kālī turns her face away; let there be a hermitage named Pāyā.
O Queen of the Gods, place this always within your heart, from ear to ear.
Emerging from the mouth of the Guru and established in the heart through the path of the ears,
the mantra-extraction (mantroddhāra) shall likewise be like water drawn upon [the ground].
One should never write down in a book this Vidyā, which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the Dakṣiṇāmnāya-Nirvāṇapada of the Śrī Vārāhī Tantra. || 15 ||
The illustrious Bhairava said:

To that Siddhanātha, who is the universal self, supremely pure, and seated within the womb of the pride of the lotus that awakens at the divine sun; by whom the moon was brought down from the midst of the great ocean to another island,
the supreme consciousness-light of the most profound contemplation.

I bow to you, the venerable syllable *Kū*, who emerges from the midst of that [reality], piercing through the great families; who causes [beings] to perceive the divine, the intermediate space, the interior of the sky, and the earth; who moves within the wheel of the netherworld (*pātāla*) and seizes all;
who, by the western transmission, destroys both time and non-time; who is eternally devoted to the bearer of the sword; whose vow is free from the distinction between duality and non-duality.
Having abandoned gain and the like along with the virtuous,
and having drunk that very essence of existence which is a mass of nectar, she sports with a rising intoxication;
salutations to that supreme Goddess of Touch, adorned with the wheel of passion.

The power known as Bhaga, which resides in the southern corner of the manifest abode, and the venerable Pūrṇapīṭha in the left corner, which causes fear to the ignorant, and Kāmarūpa in front of it; ||| p. 89a) ||| these are the seats.

Thus pervading all, Rudra-śakti, the mother of maintenance and dissolution, abides in threefold divisions; in her midst is the God of gods, whose nature is *makula*, which is primordial and independent.

Her command has become the *bindu*, which removes the fear of bound souls (*paśu*), bestows perfection, and is the nature of awakening; she is eternally moist, her own blood, ever-rejoicing in existence, always the giver of bliss, and independent.
In her midst is the divine *liṅga*, the form of the *bindu*, which produces supreme happiness and is her own nature, eternal bliss.
I bow to the one named Śrī Kubjikā, who, agitating my beautiful body there, differentiates that dual nature into sixfold aspects.
Homage to the one whose name is Nirnāman, the bestower of fortune upon the wheel of fortune.
Salutations to Ānandā and to Daivī; salutations to you who possess the form of the Bhaga.
By beholding the face of a woman during her menses, one is liberated from all sins.
By conversing with her, one obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya and other sacrifices;
by the mere touch of her, one attains the fourfold liberation.
Merely by union with her, one becomes capable of rending the three worlds;
by worshipping her with purity, [one attains] the vulva adorned with the *rajas*.

Having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon one's own body with the [mantras] of the Kula, and having worshipped the womb (yoni) with special offerings as desired, the measure of merit acquired is beyond reckoning.
With great effort, O Mistress of the Gods, the goddess Puṣpavatī, who possesses auspicious marks,
is worshipped with the understanding that she is united with the deities Piśitāli and the others.
One should drink this divine nectar of celestial light according to the prescribed rite, personally and with devotion as desired; then, O Hari, one's dullness will certainly be destroyed.
Having become one with Brahman, one should personally recite the mantra with devotion to the Queen of the Gods;
then, at the time of dismissal, after performing worship once more, one should drink the auspicious vessel again.
When this is performed through the observance [of the day], one will certainly become equal to Śiva.
O Goddess, one should guard it from others just as one guards one's own vulva.
This auspicious secret must not be revealed to a wicked son; it is to be guarded and guarded. Yet, through negligence, it may be disclosed—this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
O Goddess, the great fruit of the secret worship is difficult to attain in the three worlds;
yet a hero who recites this supreme hymn of praise with devotion attains it.
At the time of sexual union, especially, a man becomes equal to Śiva.
Thus ends this most wonderful hymn consisting of twelve verses.
It is taught that even when she is menstruating, she brings about all accomplishments;
this is the truth, the truth, again the truth—the truth of truths, there is no doubt.
Even in the world of Brahmā, such worship with flowers and offerings is difficult to find;
I am unable to describe the full majesty of this hymn.
If one recites the Virañjimadhya-Viṣṇu hymn continuously,
by the power of reciting this praise, the creation and maintenance of the universe shall certainly be established.
Therefore, with all effort, one should remember the auspicious Goddess Gopyakara,

who wears dark blue garments, who first brought flowers, whose eyes and face were filled with intoxication from the drops of blood, who held a honey-cup, who was bent by the weight of her heavy breasts, whose necklace had slipped away, and who was dark-complexioned and sweet-voiced.
She who wears a garland of twenty shimmering skulls.
The Goddess said:
"O Lord, I have heard everything in its entirety, the supreme sequence,
categorized according to its tradition, arising from the son of all the scriptures."
The essence of Tantra, the essence of Ritual, the very extensive essence of Kula,
as well as the essence of Trika, O Lord, which is the inner heart of the Yoginīs.
O Lord, the arising of Kālacakra, born from a mass of splendor,
the Yāmala, the Tamas-siddhānta, and the origin of the eight Bhairavas.
The Gāruḍa, the Bhūtatantra, and the very extensive Vidyāsāra,
as well as the arrangement of sixty-four [divisions] and their expansion, have been heard by me.
Through the division of the five streams, the Śaiva tradition is well-ascertained by scripture;
it consists of the divisions of mantra and tantra, as well as the internal division of the cakras within the heart.
Through the divisions of essence, the divisions of digits, and the divisions of the eternal, consisting of what is heard from scripture,
one attains certainty regarding Rudra-śakti, Parā-śakti, and Svarā-śakti.
The *Svacchanda* is the supreme distinction, the determination of what is higher and lower;
it is illuminated by the *Saura*, *Vaiṣṇava*, *Pauṣpa*, and the *Sāratarka*.
O Lord, having heard from you of the division consisting of the *sāṃbhava*, *āṇava*, and *śākta* [powers],
those whose minds are intent on the yoga of the ultimate reality find the affliction— which is more painful than pain— to be like nectar.
Some are devoted to the yoga of meditation, some are intent upon recitation, some are absorbed in breath control (prāṇāyāma), and others follow the sequence of the half-moon digit.

Some are devoted to the piercing of the bindu, while others are established in the supreme knowledge of the branches (śākhya-jñāna); some are intent on supreme action (parakarma), and others are established in the "opening of the eyes" (cakṣunmīlita).
Some are devoted to fire rituals, while others are devoted to sacrifices and the like;
all of them suffer, for no conviction whatsoever arises through such means, O Protector.

Without the detailed classification of the lineage, the accomplishment of the command has been revealed— the heart of the meaning of all scriptures, the most supreme among the supreme for the virtuous.
Tell me, in the compendium of the essence of the Śrī Ciñcinīmata.
Bhairava said:
This question is most secret, the inner core of the Yoginī’s heart;
it is difficult for all the gods to accomplish and must be guarded with great effort.
O fair-faced one, because you are so dear to me, I shall tell you without any doubt this essence of the Ciñcinīmata, the divine current, the supreme state.
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the supreme compendium of the essence,
the ultimate Kaula tradition of the lineage of the Siddhas, which bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
The Kula-Akula doctrine is dissolved within Bhairava, who extends to the end of the infinite void;
it is the void emerged from the universe, the mandala resting in Śakti.
Then, O Goddess, there arose the supreme Kāminī, who can assume any form at will;
she is the maiden established in the seat of Kālapīṭha, raining down the great divine current.
The Goddess said:
O Protector, how is it that I have been impelled by you toward the divine stream?
By your grace, please explain the supreme birth of good fortune.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, to the supreme secret, the compendium of all scriptures,
the subtle lineage transmission that brings about the descent of the divine Kaula.
O fair-faced one, out of affection for you, I shall tell you without doubt:
drink the divine stream of supreme bliss from the mouth of the Kaulika.
In its center arises the tree of consciousness, with roots and branches spreading far and wide;
it bears the supreme fruit of the lineage of Siddhas, mounted upon an invisible form.
The locations, the arrangement of the body, the origin of the great seats (mahāpīṭhas),
the supreme and divine mass of phonemes, and Bhairava who awakens all— [these I shall explain].
The Rudras, the Vīras, as well as the Siddhas, the Kṣatrapālas born of their own fields,
the Yoginīs, the Yogins, those ending with the Vāmas, and all the Śāstras and Kulāgamas.
Those born of the sacred seats (pīṭha), those perfected in the sacred seats, those arising from the sacred seats and the secondary seats (upapīṭha),
the assembly (saṃdoha), the divine enclosure (caṇvara), the cave-dwelling, and the deep cavern (gahvara).
Moving through the sky, abiding within that which moves in the sky, having the nature of space, and devouring the earth—
divided into one hundred million branches, the lineage tree is most extensive.
The nameless, colorless name is indeed Vāgbhava, clearly Khecarī;
beginning with the letter 'A' and ending with 'Kṣa', it is the sleeping body of bliss.
One should contemplate Kulabhairava, who resembles a wish-fulfilling gem, in his extensive form;
he is the divine abode, the transition between abodes, and his own station emerged from the recitation.
The bliss of the unmanifest form, transcending [all], belonging to the stainless lineage—
thus, O Goddess, has the determination of the sequence of the Divine Current (divyogha) been told.
To the bestower of enjoyment and liberation, who grants the fruit of the perfection of worship.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, what kind of lineage was described by you in response to my question?
O Master, if you are pleased with me, please tell it out of your grace.
Bhairavī said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the characteristic of the lineage itself— the secret doctrine, the supreme Śrī-Ciñcinīmata, which is distinct from other systems of thought.

O fair-faced one, I shall describe that which is more essential than the essence, divine, the abode of the sun and moon, the locus of being, consciousness, and insentience, and like the petal of a lotus.

O Goddess, this is the mass of both kinds of bliss, manifested through the lineage (pāraṃparya); it is the Kula that has emerged from the root of the lineage (kulāmūla) and has issued forth as Kulākula.
The Kaula is sixfold; the beings are surrounded by the six peaks, which is the eternal.
It has arisen from the six designations through the expansion of the Western Tradition.
The Goddess said:
What indeed is the designation in the West, and what is the nature of the lineage?
What are its characteristics and its causal basis, and what is the Kaula conduct?

What is the practitioner and the means of accomplishment, as well as initiation and the observance of commitments? What is the sacrificial pap and its consumption, how is the noble conduct performed, and what indeed is the nature of the vow?
Duality, as well as non-duality, and likewise both duality and non-duality—
O Lord, tell me in truth, what is the nature of the vision of the sandals?
Is it with support or without support? Is it devoid of reality or possessed of reality?
Is it with bliss or without bliss? Is it without characteristics or possessing characteristics?
Is it with form or without form? What is the nature of the final stage?
Is it Śākta, or Sāṃbhava, or indeed Jñāna-mānava alone?
O Lord, speak of the potency of mantra, its meaning, its essential nature, and likewise its arising;
as well as the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā), the net of nooses, and the melting [seal].
How is the root, and what is the continuum? What is the succession like? How are the treatise, the vigor, and the science of erotics [taught]?

Which are the seats (pīṭhas), and which are the secondary seats (upapīṭhas)? Who are the Siddhas and Yoginīs? What is the nature of the group of four, the group of five, the group of six, and the group of three?

The Foundation (Mūlādhāra), the Self-Abiding (Svādhiṣṭhāna), the Jewel-Filled (Maṇipūra), the Unstruck (Anāhata), the Pure (Viśuddhā), and likewise the Command (Ājñā)—how do these sixfold [centers] abide? How do they abide?
O Lord, what is the nature of pervasion (vyāpti), and likewise, what is the determination of its divisions?
And what is the threefold sequence consisting of the divine, the terrestrial, and the celestial?
The tree, the flower, the lineage of the cave, as well as the convention and the house;
the state of abiding, birth, and fame— what indeed is the nature of accomplishment?
O Lord, there are three authorities and likewise three lineages;
what is the difference between these six streams and the vision of the Pādukā, O Master?
The emergence from the mandala, the mandala itself, the sequence of the mandala,
and likewise the conclusion of the mandala— O Lord, there are twenty-seven mandalas.
O Lord, how is their worship performed, and what is the nature of their pervasiveness?
How is the lamp offered, and for what reason are they worshipped at the conclusion of the meal?
What is the ritual procedure and what is the argha vessel? With which substances should one perform it?
O Lord, how are you pervaded in both the higher and lower [realms] for the sake of grace and restraint?

What is the seed of the group of six fears, and what is its locus through worship? What is the sacrificial pap (caru), and what is the mudrā of desire? And of what nature is the casting of the glance?
O Lord, what is the worship in the *pādukākrama* regarding the obligatory and occasional rites?
There is the seniority of initiation (*dīkṣājyeṣṭha*), the seniority of station (*sthānajyeṣṭha*), and thirdly, the seniority of command (*ājñājyeṣṭha*).
Indeed, the fourth [offering] is superior according to the sequence; who here would not honor it?
Likewise, the lamp, the sacrificial oblation (caru), the flower, and the vessel for the respectful offering (arghapātra) follow this sequence.
To what kind of person, however, should the supreme vision of the Pādukā be given—
the [vision] that is the sequence-knowledge, the object of sequence-knowledge, the characteristic of the sequence, and the arising of the sequence?
What is the division of sequence, the flood of sequence, and that which transcends sequence?
What is the accomplishment of sequence, the practice of sequence, as well as Akula and Kula?
The nine notions, the three notions, the six notions, and likewise the five;
the three notions and the single notion—the Goddess Siddhā stands at their side.
Tell me their names, which number fifty-two according to their divisions;
O Lord, how are the festival days determined, and who is worshipped there?
By what sequence is the command bestowed upon the disciple?
What are the six flavors residing within the body, and what are the five jewels like?
O Lord, bestow vigor, the means of realization, and pervasiveness;
likewise, grant the linguistic codes, the secret signs, and the assemblies, both external and internal.
To what kind of person should the extremely rare Kaula conduct be revealed? O Lord, I ask this; tell it to me according to the true nature of the doctrine.
This very extensive question, arising from all the scriptures, has been asked so that, through your grace, my intellect may become free from delusion.
I constantly observe the ever-arisen [reality] on the unwavering Kaulika path; O son, I am eternally free from desire, devoid of attachment, and without craving for wife or children.
And I salute that which is free from old age and grey hair, and is eternal bliss.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain in great detail the *praśnakūṭa*,
which bestows the perfection of the command (*ājñāsiddhi*), is divine, and grants both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
O Goddess of the Gods, I shall describe to you the western characteristics, which generate all good fortune and bestow the fruits of all desires.

Beyond the hundred thousand, distinct from the hundred thousand, free from the side of the hundred thousand—indeed, stainless and devoid of sides—is that which is to be consumed; such is the characteristic of the house to be consumed.
O Goddess, they know that to be the Western lineage, the lineage of lineages;
it is the mental [stream] that has become exhausted, like a great ocean without waves.
He is remembered as the home of profound, deep, and impenetrable bliss;
some, devoted to their own inherent nature, abide in the arising of the primordial wheel.
Having abandoned all that distinction between south and north, as well as the arising of the sequence of the eternal Kālī, one should, by means of one's own nature, dissolve into that Western Abode.

The speaker and the one who speaks, the active and the inactive, the poet and the poetry, the lineage and the non-lineage, the wheel and the one who turns the wheel, the sequence and the desireless, the cave and the one who hides within it— these are the heart and the rest.
Having understood the meaning of the lineage transmission, one should worship Vimalabhairava,
the western bliss of arising, which is the certainty of the generation stage.
O lady of excellent vows, the secret of the Siddha tradition has been told to you; O most beloved one, I shall now further declare another concerning the lineage.

He who knows the triple family, that which transcends the triple family, the three realms of existence, that which is beyond the three realms of existence, and that which is devoid of the womb within the triple womb— he indeed belongs to the lineage of Ambā.
Desiring desire, she assumes this form; she is that form who adorns the lineage.
She is consciousness and the unconscious, the womb of *Ciñcinī*, truly pure and perfected.
O Goddess, he who knows that bearer of the command, who is intent upon restraint and grace,
and who is intensely and most intensely [devoted], should be known as one who possesses the lineage.
He who knows the intoxication that lies between the states of the drunkard and the sober, which transcends intoxication yet arises from it—
having experienced that intoxication, he who knows that divine intoxication is a true follower of the lineage.
O Goddess, this supreme characteristic of the Manvayī has been declared by me;
now I shall further proclaim another, the most excellent characteristic of the Guru.
By which one may awaken the Veda, the source of all scriptures—
that Brahman which is subtler than the subtlest and the cause of all causes.
That reality is beyond qualities and beginningless; it has neither a higher nor a lower state.
It is devoid of all beginnings, all states of existence, and all enjoyments.
It is the awakening to all time and the state of perfect savoring of the six tastes;
it is that for which there is no grasping at nirvāṇa, nor any abandoning in the ocean of existence.
One who abides through the yoga of contact with these two is called a Guru;
such is the great secret, because the Guru awakens one to all purposes.
He is called a Guru for the purpose of investigating delusive cognition;
furthermore, I shall now declare another such supreme characteristic.
Endowed with all auspicious marks, an investigator of all scriptures,
possessed of compassion for all beings, he is compassionate by nature and affectionate toward his disciples.
If he is a teacher, skillful, tranquil in mind, and of noble birth;
an ascetic, observer of vows, a dweller in caves, and one who has conquered his senses.
He is Kālacakra, yet not subject to becoming; he subsists on alms and possesses the form of a hero.
He is the lineage-holder of the Kulokālā-kula tradition and an investigator of the Krama scriptures.
One who has received the initiation of piercing (vedhadīkṣā), possesses awakened consciousness, is renounced, is steadfast,
devoted to the Supreme, free from agitation, and knows the true character— such is the characteristic of a Guru.
I shall further proclaim another supreme means of conviction regarding the Guru:
the deity Siddhakhecarī, whose form is invisible and who is peaceful.
O beloved, those with divine vision behold the movement of the Three-eyed One,
as well as the dispeller of the fever of desire and the entry into another's body.
Penetration into another and the drawing forth of another—such is the conviction regarding the Guru. O Goddess, this has been declared by me as the definition of the conviction regarding the Guru.
I shall further proclaim the unsurpassed Kaula conduct,
which is the door to the castes, the door to progeny, and the stainless door to liberation.
This supreme division, the divine Kaula conduct, has been proclaimed.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, how is the door of the castes [varṇa], and how is the door of the subjects [prajā] remembered?
O Mahādeva, O Nirañjana, tell me of the door of liberation.
Please, out of your grace, explain this fourfold division.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the supreme secret of the Kaula tradition,
the fourfold lineage that bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
The sun of awakening, delighted by the union of the final vowel and the nasal sound (anusvāra),
having attained the form of resonance, is supported in the center of the palate.
Through the flow of the life-force thread (prāṇasūtra), it is conjoined with the fifty phonemes;
it is Vaikharī, the yoker of the mouth, and born from the lineage of the Vīrāvalī.
O Goddess, this Kulabhairava, with a wide-open mouth and radiant, has emerged;
thus have I declared to you this unsurpassed gateway of the letters.
It brings forth progeny and delights the mind; it is overflowing with the bliss of flowing [nectar];
it is threefold, consisting of thirty-nine [deities], and the mandala of the sequence is likewise threefold.
O Goddess, that divine [lotus], submerged in the nectar of the Aghora [mantra] and throbbing with consciousness and unconsciousness in its center,
is proclaimed as the mouth of the Trimūrti and the gateway to progeny.
Situated within the navel-cakra is the circle of light consisting of consciousness and matter;
it is the supreme, divine Great Womb (Mahāyoni), which illumines the Brahma-nāḍī.
Then, by means of an upward flow, one should pierce the palate-path, which is all-pervasive and facing in every direction,
and cause the nectar of consciousness to melt.
O auspicious one, I declare this to be the stainless gateway to liberation;
it resides in the center of the Śiva-maṇḍala and is the arising of the sequence of Mahākālī.
Therein, I spoke of Udyogā, Carcitā, and Viropakā; I have also taken up Mahāsaṃhārasaṃhārā and Kulārṇavā.
Stainless, omnipresent, the speaker of all languages as a single speech,
reaching from the end of the great kalpa to the end of the kalpa, he has entered the dissolution into Great Śiva.
The hero who bears great splendor, beloved by those dear to him;
the perfected one who has attained the state of a great adept; the mandala of the great divine flood.
This sequence, which is beyond description and within the sphere of the yoginīs' realization,
is proclaimed as the Kaula conduct, divided into four parts.
He who knows the divine sequence shall be a guru who bestows liberation. Furthermore, O Dear One, I shall explain another matter: the practice for the adept.
Wherever the yogi’s state of being has been completely exhausted and he has attained absorption into that, there he remains, transformed by the supreme state beyond manifestation.
And he beholds the supreme vision; whatever object is desired by the mind is obtained instantly, for that inner self is such by its very nature.
O Dear One, when joy and sorrow have been abandoned and one has become steady upon the surface of the earth, that practice brings success to the practitioner.
Freed from all associations, he remains there, self-satisfied;
there, O beloved, he experiences the pure, cultivated yoga of rest.
O Dear One, one perceives one's own family, the reality, the differentiation of other states, the travel through supreme space, and the accomplishment or non-accomplishment of the practice.
O Goddess, by the casting of a glance and the observation [of the target], the mudrā causes bursting;
likewise, it effects the animation of an image and the burning of a cloth-painting.
The sādhana of the yakṣiṇī, the dissolution, the wind-storm,
the bursting of stones, earthquakes, mantra, meditation, and the power of moving through the sky.
O Goddess, it effects the attraction of living beings, destroys the thoughts of others,
enables entry into cities, and causes madness, O Beloved.
O Goddess, it serves to destroy untimely death and ward off the disease of fever; O Beloved, having made the body firm, it is the means for paralyzing speech.
Having performed the mastery of distant hearing, one hears the weeping of living beings;
likewise, having performed the stopping of movement, one effects the blazing of fire without fuel.
It draws in the hosts of birds and the sky, and wards off yakṣas and bhūtas;
thus, O Goddess, has the practice of Yogeśvara been described.
I shall further proclaim another initiation, the supreme Kaulika initiation;
it consists of the mantra-initiation with its seed-syllables, and an oblation of clarified butter, unrefined ghee, food, and sesame seeds.

O Dear One, the Kaulika initiation is seedless; it is a piercing [of the centers] by means of the nature of the Self, having brought about the manifestation of the True Reality, and resting within the internal space.
O Goddess, staying there, one should meditate upon Ājñā Vimalabhairava; O Dear One, this is the means of transmission that causes the body of the bound soul (paśu) to swell.
It is filled with the joy and bliss of the supreme self’s own awakening;
yet, when joined with the distinctions of conceptual construction, it is the stainless body of the bound soul (paśu).
By means of the very process of "hā-hā" (the cry of lament), they gradually relaxed their physical forms;
through that very method of reasoning, they took refuge in the consciousness of the letter *Kā*.

Having drunk the nectar of *Akula*, which is permeated by the realization of its own intrinsic nature, one experiences the arising of the essence within the hollow of the *kaka* through the method of yogic application.
With the flood of his wings spread wide on both sides, overflowing with the state of his own bliss,
he bathed his body with the sound of laughter that issued forth.
O Goddess of the lords of gods, the initiation by piercing (vedhadīkṣā) has been described according to one's own realization;
it severs the fear of saṃsāra and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Furthermore, I shall proclaim another commitment (samaya) in the Kaulika tradition:
from Brahmā down to the lowest outcaste, all castes are established [within it].
The Supreme Self, the Supreme Power, the conscious path, is fully realized;
having attained a mind established in equanimity, one abides in purity with senses in a state of balance.
Moving within all beings and manifesting in animal and human forms,
wherever he appears through his power, there indeed is his dissolution.
The inner self, the omniscient one, renowned as the void whose nature is the void,
endowed with all forms and attributes, is the Lord of the Samaya.
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter in the Dakṣiṇāmnāya section of the Nirvāṇapada within the Śrī Vārāhī Tantra.
Bhairava said:
O fair-faced one, I shall further proclaim that which is the essence of essences:
the beautiful sacrificial oblation (caru) and likewise the characteristics of the vow for the preceptor.
For the lord of yogis, endowed with devotion, intent on wandering through sacred sites,
united with the Supreme Reality, and dedicated to the Kaula vow;
One should undertake the practice of begging for alms for the sake of sacrifice within the circle of living beings;
one should be constantly devoted to the practice of yoga and always delight in the sequential worship.
The word of the Guru, which is the support of command and characterized by the secret convention (*sailisaṃketa*),
brings about for him, O Goddess, the Kaulika accomplishment that bestows liberation.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, what is the nature of the *caru* offering, and what is the nature of the "six beyond"?
O Lord, please explain to me the sequence of the practice of vows and the inner science (*adhyātma*).
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the six-fold characteristics of the other [tradition],
the supreme Western lineage, which is joined with the practice of vows.
The lake is devoid of the six waves, adorned with the six categories (ṣaṭpadārtha),
resting within the six internal positions, and possessing the supreme essence of the transcendence of the fast.
The supreme path of liberation is like the white and black fortnights;
it is joined with the spark of the *praṇava*, the ultimate lineage of the West.
The supreme fragment of the cosmic egg is proclaimed to be beyond the ether;
through the practice of experiential instruction, it is the most excellent abode of bliss.
And while situated within the sound of *hālā*,
one who has made the vital breath his life-force should maintain the divine *parāmṛta-caru* (the sacrificial oblation of supreme nectar).
O lady of excellent hips, the characteristics of one who observes the vow have been told;
now I shall further explain another [topic], namely the dualistic and non-dualistic characteristics.
Wherever the arising of Kālacakra occurs— whether it be the state of space, beyond the state of space, one’s own state, or within another state— there the Supreme is consumed.
Thus, O Goddess, through this sequential analysis, the characteristic of duality-and-non-duality and the vision of the sandals have been told to me in their true essence.
O Goddess, that reality which is meditated upon from the beginning, middle, and end of the *bindu* and *nāda*,
having become a state of equal flavor (*samarasa*) with duality, is proclaimed as non-duality (*advaita*).
I shall further declare another question that is extremely difficult to obtain:
Is it with support or without support? Is it devoid of reality, or is it possessed of reality?
Is it with joy or without joy? Is it without characteristics or with characteristics? Is it with form or without form? What is the nature of the final stage?
Abiding in the space of consciousness with its own form as the bliss of the second bindu, what could it perceive with an object? But being without an object, it abandons even that.
Meditation is that by which the object of meditation is cultivated until it becomes clearly manifest within the field of perception;
it is proclaimed as the reality that is ever-vibrant, eternally arising as bliss, and constant.
And that which they say is the eternal Supreme, whose form is the dissolution of all beings, the bliss of the equal flavor of everything— that is proclaimed as the fifth *tat*.

One should know that bliss to be the arising from the churning of consciousness and the unconscious, born from the essence of one's own true nature; whereas that mind which is devoid of bliss is indeed joyless.
One should know that to be the signless, wherein the all-pervading, subtle form has been dissolved; I shall now describe that sign.
One should practice with the supreme intellect the supreme light, which is the radiance of consciousness;
when it is seen by that supreme vision, it is called "with support" (sālamba).

One should know that to be with form by which the moving and the unmoving are pervaded through the principles (tattvas), the supreme Kalās, and Time; however, one should abandon that which is formless.
O Goddess of the gods, O beloved, I shall further proclaim the characteristics of the Śākta, the Sāmbhava, and the Mānava [initiations], which bring about the arising of great knowledge.
Will, knowledge, action, as well as the supreme Kuṇḍalinī,
and Mātṛkā as the fifth— this is held to be the pentad of powers (śakti).
Knowledge arising from the expansion of desire is the vision therein;
it is the performance of what is to be done and what is not to be done, as well as the awakening of Kuṇḍalinī.
The universe is embraced by the Mātṛkā, which is characterized by the fivefold power;
and one who is fully realized in the supreme state perceives the nature of the Self as the power of consciousness.
O Goddess, by means of the differentiation of supports, those who rely on the various branches of the Kula rest one in another, moving from one station to another.

O Goddess, that which is meditated upon as having a separate division and a separate establishment, existing in a state of duality—this has been described by me; it is proclaimed as the *āṇava* [impurity].
The Goddess said:
O Lord, how is there a support? How can there be separate accomplishment?
Through the distinction of the yoga of repose, there is a separate location and a separate sequence.
Please speak out of your grace, so that there may be a worthy recipient for this accomplishment.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain the extensive knowledge of the branches (śākhājñāna),
which is cultivated through its own power as distinct accomplishments and distinct divisions.

O Goddess of the gods, it has been told to you: this shall yield the fruit of all accomplishments (siddhi), as well as the support (ādhāra), the contraction (saṃkoca), and likewise the fourth birth (turyajanma).
O Goddess, Kaṇḍa, Kuṇḍalinī, and likewise that which is called Kumbha;
then the station Sañjīvanī, Bhūtālā, and Jīvasampuṭa.
Kurmodhāra, Sparśaga, the one called Lola, Laṃvikodara, Guruvaktra, and likewise, O Goddess, Añjavaktra.
And the supreme state of purity is considered to be beyond emission;
likewise, O Goddess, that which ends with emission—these are proclaimed as the sixteen.
I shall now describe these sixteen separately established supports for the sake of rising upward; the venomous serpents [serve as] their foundations, and the mountains are their own abodes.
O Dear One, standing upon the support of all, he causes the entire earth to tremble;
having drawn in all the worlds, he moves about within the netherworld (pātāla).
Stationed at the point of contraction, one will undoubtedly paralyze all armies;
one shall destroy the wicked minds and uproot every tree.
When practiced, it takes away the pride of the serpents; when nourished by the wind, it causes all to flee and brings the moving and the unmoving under one's control.
One who is well-established in the wheels of birth attains supreme good fortune;
she can move statues and the like, and attract the wives of wise men.
Leaping through the expanse of the sky, the yogin, supported by the wheel of the *kanda*,
mounted upon the foundation of the *kuṇḍalinī*, shall summon the host of *yoginīs*.
One should pierce through the arguments of opponents and accomplish whatever is desired;
such a practitioner fulfills the entire universe, for his own power is indeed invincible.
One situated in the *kumbha* [sign] should perform the transference of all [consciousness]; it does not go elsewhere.
It effects the withdrawal of the rain of mental agitation and the destruction of untimely death.
The Saṃjīvanī [power] brings about self-awakening through the initiation of piercing (vedhadīkṣā);
established in the samādhi of the tortoise-support, the yogi shall enter the city of another.
O Beloved, whether with pain or without pain, without pain or with pain,
the practitioner whose mind is fixed on yoga remains established in the support of the hollow of the living soul.
He attains everything as his final goal and becomes a lord of all accomplishments;
having reached the place called Lolā, he enjoys various kinds of pleasures.
The practitioner quickly attains [success]; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
A yogi situated at the end of the *laṃvikā* (uvula) should cast off hunger and thirst.
The practitioner, free from desire, obtains the perfected elixir of mercury (rasāyana) and becomes a conqueror of death; this resides within the secret cave of the Guru’s mouth.
Having become one whose body is indestructible, he attains the supreme state;
Mahādeva, established in the equinox (visuva), is capable of uplifting the world.
There is no doubt that you will become one worshipped by the hosts of Yoginīs;
established in the state of emission (vaisargika), you shall obtain qualities such as omniscience and the rest.
O Lord, may the yogi become a destroyer and a creator, just like Sadāśiva;
may he possess knowledge of the minds of others and of the past and the future.
The practitioner truly knows the weeping of all beings according to their actual state;
likewise, he perceives the emissions, the postures, and the tremors, free from bodily constraints.
Free from all defects and blemishes, he shines in the sky like the sun;
the hero, the lord of all desires, is surrounded by the yoginīs.
"Filled with the essence of its own bliss, it sports with infinite splendor.
Thus has the nature of Śiva, as conceived by Hara, been described to you by me.

O Goddess, for the sake of the welfare of heroes, I shall explain the Yoga of the Sixteen Supports, which possesses the single characteristic of one's own prosperity and produces immediate conviction.
One should always keep this secret so that others do not perceive it;
furthermore, I shall describe the characteristics of the Śāmbhava [initiation] itself.
Equanimity (sama), movement (gata), dissolution (laya), and awakening (avabodha) constitute the fourth state;
this fourfold division is proclaimed as the Śāmbhava [state].
Bhairava said:
I shall further proclaim another secret, difficult to find on earth:
the potency of mantra, its deliberation, its essential nature, and likewise its arising.
I shall now declare this supreme, divine question, as well as its defining characteristic:
it is the state of knowing all through contemplation, the protection that bestows grace upon those in saṃsāra.
It is called *mantra* because it possesses the nature of protecting through reflection;
its root is the all-pervading Power (*śakti*), which is to be grasped as the fundamental source.
Its form is filled with that mass, possessing great pervasiveness and the arising of the supreme;
it is the risen king of mantras, whose nature is that very potency.
Having reflected upon that meaning and recollecting the king of mantras, one should practice;
for this is the means of accomplishment from accomplishment, O Goddess, otherwise one becomes like an insentient object.
O fair-faced one, I shall further proclaim another [mudrā]:
having opened the eyes that arise from the vision of the supreme *svasvarūpa*.
And having placed the bride’s joined palms, which had reached the navel, upon his heart as he meditated,
the bride [assumed] the Khecarī Mudrā, which dissolves the net of bonds.
The pacifier of all the wicked and the destroyer of all obstacles—
by honoring her, all the deities beginning with Brahmā, as well as the Yoginīs, are pleased.
O Bhairavī, the Khecarīs, the Siddhamātṛs, and the Mātṛkā-yoginī dance here and bestow accomplishment upon him.
O Goddess of gods, O beloved, at the time of worship, for him who binds the Khecarī Mudrā while beholding the Pādukā, liberation shall certainly occur.
Furthermore, O fair-faced one, the descent of the root has been described:
she who, abiding within the *bhaga*, takes the form of the *bhaga* and is the manifestation of the *bhaga*.
Bhagadrāvaka is in the womb, while Mūlasthānī is established in the other.
The Goddess said:
But how is it that "bhaga" is spoken of? Of what kind is it?
Out of grace, please tell me of this divine lineage of Bhaganityā.
Bhairava said:
Listen, O Goddess; I shall proclaim the definitive conclusion regarding Bhagannityā. Out of affection for you, O fair-faced one, I shall tell it to you without any doubt.
The Bhaga is renowned as a triangle, a secret mandala situated within the intellect;
it consists of the corners of Will, Knowledge, and Action, and in its center is the sequence of Ciñcinī.
Emerging from the ocean of space, she is the embodiment of bliss through her own radiance;
she is the delighter of all, eternally satisfied, and the form of the womb (bhaga).
She is the mother of the universe, the devourer of time, and the powerful one;
having drunk the essence of desire, she is pure, eternal, and has the form of the yoni.
She resides within the void of the sky-faring digit; she is the devourer of the lunar digit in the void.
Therefore, intoxicated by her devotion to the drink, that eternal one has the form of the yoni (bhaga).
The seedless one possesses the state of being a seed; she takes form through the emergence from her own seed.
Situated within Kulakaula, she is eternal and has the form of the Bhaga.
When neither contraction nor expansion exists for the swan [of the mind] within the mechanism,
then eternal bliss arises for one whose consciousness is dissolved therein.
The solar fire is churned by the wheel, and the lunar Kula flows forth;
that which is satisfied without union is the eternal one, whose form is the Bhaga.
O Mahācakriṇī, at the union of the *bhaga* and the *liṅga*,
that eternal one whose form is the *bhaga* stands quivering there in the center.
Tasting the cotton-wool [of the seed] with her mouths within the womb, she is the sprout of consciousness;
that eternal one, whose form is the womb, has caused the universe to melt.
She who dissolves the minds of others when one has entered another's body,
having drawn them to her own plane, she is eternal and possesses the form of Bhaga.
She who is the source of all functions and so forth, she who possesses the threefold division and the triple womb;
she who is of three kinds and has three ears, she is the eternal one whose form is the *bhaga*.
Thus, O Goddess, has the definitive teaching on the Bhagamūla been told;
now I shall speak again of another question that is most difficult to obtain.
But as for the lineage in succession, O fair-faced one, I shall describe it:
where there is the arising of the Kula-hero, there is the mandala of the assembly of heroes.
O Śiva, that sun of awakening has arisen from within the void of the void;
from Bhāskara was born Ravi, and from Ravi was born Divākara.
The world, which is the interior of the lotus that is the womb of the sun,
is praised as being composed of consciousness; it is the light of both the conscious and the unconscious, all-pervading, and the seed-vitality of Śiva.
Abiding within all beings, it is proclaimed as the lineage;
it is both the Krama and the Cakrāmaka, the Krama emerged from the Ogha.
The sequence is the flood, the continuum established in the state beyond conduct;
it is the abandonment of the six sense-faculties, the weapon, the divine flood, and the maṇḍala.
That which is the place for contemplating its inner essence, wherein they find rest and delight—that is renowned as the scripture; one should bow to that compendium of the web of speech.
Furthermore, O Goddess, I have explained the definitive determination of the seed-syllable itself,
as well as the expansion of its retinue and limbs, which is devoid of names and castes.
Thus, the root mantra is remembered; it is the concise method of accomplishment, which, having abandoned the state of sound, abides in the form of pure awareness.
Abiding as the seed-creation, it is completely filled with the supreme bliss of consciousness;
the Vidyā is pregnant with the inner self, bestowing its own self-luminosity.
It possesses the potency of its own seed-mantra and brings about the exhaustion of birth and karma;
it is renowned for its non-lucid color and is devoid of the throat, palate, and lips.
The face of the *argha* is not to be uttered; the syllable never decays anywhere.
It is neither black nor protective; that color is proclaimed as such.
I shall now further proclaim the sacred seats (pīṭha) and the protection of the lords of the seats:
first is the Kaulika seat, and second is the Vinayakaula seat.
The third is Siddhakaula, while Divyakaula is the fourth;
the first is the group of sixteen, and the second is that beginning with 'ka' and ending with 'sa'.
The third is that beginning with *yā* and ending with *phā*; the fourth is the *Rūhama*.
The seat (*pīṭha*) called Soma belongs to Kaulinī, while the solar seat is Vinayakaulika.
Siddhakaula, likewise Āgneya, that which is called Vidyā, and Divyakaulika—these are established within the self; now I shall describe them to you externally.
Śrīśaila, Śrī Mahendra, Candra-dvīpa, and Kailāsa— O fair-faced goddess, these four, O Goddess, are proclaimed as the seats of Śiva (śivapīṭha).
And I shall proclaim the Pīṭhas, which bestow the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation:
Candra, Kumāraśikhara, and Mahānanda as the fourth.
It is secret, most secret, and divine, proclaimed as the Lord of the Pīṭha;
listen, O lady of excellent vows, for I shall speak of it for the sake of the Siddhas and Yoginīs.
The support (ādhāra), one's own wheel (svacakra), and the lord of the deer (kuraṅgīśa) are proclaimed;
O Queen of the Gods, that which is named Madanda is proclaimed as the perfected seat (pīṭhasiddha).
Raktā, Kalālā, Caṇḍākṣī, Mahocchuṣmā, and Caturthikā— these,
established in the sacred seats (pīṭha), have been declared by me as the goddesses who possess the Kaulika form.
Bhairava said:
I shall further proclaim the unsurpassed sequence of worship:
the fourfold, the fivefold, the sixfold, and the threefold Supreme Lord.
O Dear One, I shall describe the fourfold group, both external and internal:
intellect is the first seat, and mind is the second.
The third seat (pīṭha) should indeed be Ahaṃkāla, which is Unmana.
Oṃkārapīṭha is the first; Jālapīṭha is the second;
Pūrṇapīṭha shall be the third; and Devapīṭha is Kāmarūpa.
These are the seats (pīṭhas) consisting of power, both external and internal;
they should be worshipped according to the prescribed rite, together with the Siddhas and Yogis.
Oṃānanda, likewise Siddhānanda as the second,
Kulananda as the third, and Candragarbha as the fourth.
O Goddess of gods, the name of Pūjā is Devīputra, who is born of her mind;
[the others are] Raktākṣī, Tārā, Jihvā, Karākṣī, and Somajihvikā.
Caṇḍākṣī, Agnijihvā, Ucchuṣmā,
and Sūryajihvikā are to be worshipped according to the ritual procedure as they have emerged from the mouth of the Guru, O Dear One.
The group of four has been described, O Goddess; now hear that group of five from the Goddess:
Anādi (the Beginningless), Sarvajñatā (Omniscience), Devī (the Goddess), Muktā (the Liberated), and Yogeśvarī (the Mistress of Yoga).
The *samarī* is known as *siddha-saṃjñā*, and the *kubjikā* is remembered as *samayī*.
O Goddess, the pentad has been explained; now listen, O beloved, to the sixfold yoga (*yoga-ṣaṭka*).
Then, O fair-faced one, Vimalā, Prakārā, Kubjikā and the others,
Mātaṅgī, Sikhinī, Īśvarī, Suhirā, Ānandā, and Sundarī.

The group of six known as the *nugraha* has been declared; now listen, O beloved, to the group of six knowledges (*jñāna-ṣaṭka*). O Goddess, the Command (*ājñā*) consists of Kubjikā, Māṃtagī, and Śuddhā.
Anāhata and Mālinī are in Maṇipūra, Khageśvarī in Svādhiṣṭhāna, Jihvā in the heart, and Vijihvrikā in the Ādhāra.
The sixfold knowledge has been declared; now listen, O lady of excellent vows, to the three throats.
By means of the division of the lineage, the Supreme Pervasive One is the triple form.
O Bhairavī, one should worship him who stands on the bank, joined with two [vowels] and having one on the left;
O Goddess, likewise [one should offer] "Oṃ Miṣaṃ," and again "Oṃ Vali" three times.
O blessed lady, this new convention is obtained from the mouth of the Guru;
likewise, one should worship the lineage of Gurus, such as it is in this tradition.
Relying upon the root of the rootless, vibrate within that which is known as the Command (ājñā).
Therein lies that which is renowned as the Śrīkrama, the beloved of the Yoginīs.
That sequence has been declared, known as the Five Jewels;
the Triad has also been told, O Goddess; now hear the sixfold variety.
The Ādhāra is said to be Guḍa, while Svādhiṣṭhāna is the Liṅga;
Maṇipūra extends to the navel, and Anāhata is in the heart.
The pure [center] is in the region of the throat, while the Ājñā is situated between the eyebrows. O beloved, I shall further declare another secret question within.
O Goddess of gods, O beloved, there is a threefold determination of the sequence— divine, terrestrial, and atmospheric— and the nine secret signs (saṃketaka) on the back of the vessel.
O fair-faced one, one should worship with supreme devotion this very divine [mandala];
the detailed sequence of worship has already been described in the section on the fourfold [arrangement].
One should worship within the outer mandala according to one's means;
one should know this to be Bhaumanta, which bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
I shall further proclaim another auspicious sequence of the intermediate space (antarikṣa)—
the sky-traveler situated within the sky-traveler, whose nature is space, the supreme space.
O Supreme Goddess, one should also worship the blazing Great Wheel, the Wheel of Time (Kālacakra) which is further augmented by splendor and arises through the sequential unfolding (kramodaya).
Consisting of twelve rays, possessing a brilliance equal to the vast sun,
it is meditated upon through the realization of the supreme awakening as having the nature of space.
O Beloved, having worshipped the sky-flower mandala with the Kha-mudrā in the lineage,
one should worship the other state of the void (kha-padāntara) through the experience of the essential nature of the void.
Seated upon the seat of the space between the birds, I worship the solar orb where rest is found— the rays of the sky,
whose bliss has overflowed from the power of consciousness (cicchakti).
Thus, O Goddess, has the auspicious sequence of the intermediate space been described.
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the Dakṣiṇāmnāya section of the Nirvāṇapada within the Śrī Vārāhī Tantra. || 17 ||
Bhairava said:
